### **INTRODUCTION** 

Copper pyrometallurgical smelting technology comprises mainly three stages, i.e. smelting, converting and refining. 

Copper refining processes, both pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical, are simple and mature. The typical process for Cu pyrometallurgical refining uses rotary anode furnace which uses porous brick, no (or insufficient) oxidation reduction and dilute oxygen combustion technology. Its operation efficiency and energy consumption are improving. Large-capacity Cu electrolyzing process uses stainless-steel permanent cathode copper, with advanced machines and designated cranes, which has been widely recognized and applied. Copper electrolytic cell made by low shirinkage vinylester resin concrete will also be gradually popularized; while parallel-current electrolyzing technology, with higher current density, lower steam consumption, higher productivity, lower capital cost, yet 1/3 more power consumption, still needs time to be accepted by the market. Solution purification, combining traditional electrowinning and cyclone electrowinning technologies, will become the trend for future development. 

Copper smelting centers and focuses on the smelting stage and the converting stage. 

With dozens of years of d

evelopment, especially in recent decade, Cu smelting technologies are maturing, and Cu converting technologies are developing and improving. 

### **CU CONCENTRATE SMELTING** 

Cu pyrometallurgical smelting technology is divided into two categories: bath smelting technology and flash smelting technology. 

### **Flash Smelting Technology (Turbulent Suspension Smelting Technology)** 

Outokumpu flash smelting technology (Finland) and INCO flash smelting technology (Canada) are typical under this category. Among them, Outokumpu flash smelting technology is applied more extensively. Xiangguang Copper Co., Ltd, a Chinese company in Shandong Province, has conducted audacious improvement and innovation on the central jet distributer on the flash smelting furnace, and based on turbulance and pulsing theory, has invented Turbulent Suspension Smelting Technology, which was then awarded with national patent for invention by Chinese government. With this improvement, the heat load of reaction shaft is lowered and concentrate throughput is increased. Flash smelting technology is featured with advanced, mature and reliable technology, larger concentrate throughput, longer furnace life, higher automation level, 

_Proceeding of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

899 

better environmental and operation conditions. Yet it also has many deficiencies: it has complicated raw material pre-treatment process, which requires deep drying of concentrates and fine grain size of fluxes and other auxiliary materials, and higher dust rate; Since flash furnace structure is complicated with large demand of copper cooler jacket, capital cost per ton of concentrate is high; Metallurgical reaction of Flash Smelting or Turbulent Suspension Smelting technology is realized instantly with deep dried materials suspending in the reaction shaft, while molten bath is relatively stable, therefore, its impurity removal efficiency is lower than that of bath smelting technology. Moreover, ESP dusts of flash furnace could not have open-circuit handling; therefore, impurities like Pb and Zn will enter into smelting slag or tailings without effective recovery. In this regard, Flash Smelting technology has high demand on concentrate quality (about 25% Cu). Concentrates with complex composition, high impurity content and low Cu content (<20%) are not suitable for Flash Smelting technology, especially the Double Flash Technology, i.e., Flash Smelting + Flash Converting technology. 

### **Bath Smelting Technology** 

There are many types of bath smelting technologies, such as Enriched Oxygen Top-blowing Submerged Bath Smelting Technology, Mistubishi Continuous Cu Smelting Technology, Rotary Side-blowing Technology (Noranda process, Teniente process), Fixed Side-blowing Technology (Vanukov process, Baiyin process, Jinfeng process, etc.) and Enriched Oxygen Bottom-blowing Cu Smelting Technology, etc. 

### <u>Noranda Process and Teniente Process</u> 

Noranda process was originated in Canada, which are

not widely applied, mainly because it has low air pressure with need for tuyere punching, loud noise, short tuyere life, low enriched oxygen concentration (40%), high air leakage at furnace openings, high off-gas volume, low SO2 density and high fuel rate and limited capacity. Noranda furnace at Daye Smelter in China has been shut down. 

Teniente process was developed by Codelco, which was only adopted in some Latin American countries, Thailand and Zambia. Teniente furnace structure resembles Noranda furnace. Their difference lie in the concentrate drying and injecting technology: for Teniente furnace, dry concentrates are injected directly from furnace side into bath, while for Noranda furnace, wet concentrates are fed from the end of thrower, therefore, dust rate for Teniente furnace is lower (0.8%), and could realize autogenous smelting at 40% of enriched oxygen concentration with low rate of coal injection. Teniente furnace has also inherited other disadvantages of Noranda furnace. Their biggest advantage is

900 

that the smelting slag contains high Fe/SiO2 (1.7-1.8)[1], therefore slag quantity is small, and the slag could go through floatation process to gain high Cu recovery rate. Teniente people is also improving their slag cleaning method to change from Teniente slag cleaning furnace with pulverized coal as reductant to slag floatation. 

<u>Enriched-oxygen Top-blowing Submerged Bath Smelting Technology (ISA Process and Ausmelt Process)</u> 

Enriched-oxygen Top-blowing Submerged Bath Smelting Technology, represented by ISA process and Ausmelt process, was originated in Australia, and applied widely all around the world, with more than 40 smelters all over the world, 10 of which are from China (with more than 12 furnaces, including converters). This technology is featured with wide feed adaptation, flexible operation and capacity.  However, since concentrates are pelletized to decrease dust rate, moisture content is high (10-11%), and oxygen concentration is 40-60%, which make it impossible for autogenous smelting, and require 3-5% of coal for heat addition and control of magnetic iron reduction in slag. Lance is submerged in the slag layer, so foaming slag is likely to be formed, and lance life is only 3-15 days. It also requires high elevation of building. Its biggest restriction is that topblowing furnace is round and vertically arranged, with less melt volume and intense agitation, with no settling zone, and there is need for another settling (electric) furnace. Slag contains low Fe/SiO2 (1.1-1.3) [1]，and quantity is large. Cu in discarded electric furnace slag is high (0.6-0.8%), so Cu recovery rate is low. If use further floatation for the electric furnace slag, the total energy consumption will be higher, and the total Cu recovery is still not as high as that of Noranda, Teniente and Oxygen Bottom-blowing Furnace which uses high Fe/SiO2-containing slag.

Mitsubishi Cu smelting process was invented in Japan and applied in a limited number in the world, due to various reasons. The capacity for this process is normally 200,000-300,000t/a Cu. It is the only technology in the world which has realized direct flow of hot melt from smelting to converting and then to refining, thus the real continuous Cu smelting process. Anode scraps return to converting furnace, where the enriched-oxygen concentration is -35% and could treat some scraps, therefore, heat can be recycled and utilized. Dried concentrates, together with enriched oxygen, are fed from one end of burner to the bath of Smelting Furnace (S furnace), matte and slag produced enters to Cleaning Furnace (CL furnace), and matte flows to Converting Furnace (C furnace). CL furnace slag, after granulation, is discarded, which contains Fe/SiO2 1.25, and Cu of 0.7%, thus slag quantity is large and Cu recovery rate is low. This

### <u>Vanukov Process (including Jinfeng furnace)</u> 

Vanukov Side-blowing Smelting Furnace is characterized with high hearth, little splashing at feeding port and furnace opening, low dust rate, copper cooling jacket at furnace slag line, long furnace life, wide adaptability of feed, simple feed preparation, low wind pressure, high enriched oxygen concentration (60-80%), deep bath (2300mm), and high melt temperature (1250-1300℃). It uses singular furnace with partition wall inside the furnace, therefore, Cu in final slag from one furnace is low (0.6-0.8%), metal recovery rate is high. Yet as restricted by furnace structure, this technology is more suitable for middle and small sized copper smelters. Though in China there is improvedVanukov furnace type by adding two-stage furnace slag cleaning, i.e. add DC electrode on slag tapping side at the partition wall, and then slag is fed to electric furnace for further cleaning. In this case, as reported, Cu in discarded slag can be decreased to 0.47%[2] (when matte grade is 50-55%Cu), yet Fe/SiO2 is as low as 1.1-1.2, so slag quantity is large and copper recovery rate is low. If there is no electric furnace for cleaning of smelting slag,  and converting slag are conveyed together for floatation, there is no operational experience whether high Fe/SiO ~~2~~ slag can be produced from the smelting furnace. Since enriched oxygen is blown to the slag layer, matte layer is relatively stable. Though coal or coke powder is used as reducttant, there is risk of magnetic iron settling at furnace bottom to form accretion and affect operation. Like many bath smelting technologies, since enriched oxygen is blown in the slag layer, there is also risk of foaming slag for this technology. During normal operation, coal feeding rate is controlled at 3-5% for Fe3O4 reduction, and tuyere is 100mm below melt furnace. Automation le

vel is low, since when there is power shut-down, there is need for manual tuyere punching with rod, and when power is on, there is also need for manual tuyere opening. Furthermore, since there is large quantity of copper cooling jacket applied on the furnace, which carries away a lot of heat, it is far from being called as de facto autogenous smelting (though coal is mainly used for slag reduction). 

Enriched-oxygen bottom-blowing Cu smelting technology is a technology with Chinese intellectual property, whose industrialized development and application opened up a new era for Cu smelting technology. It adopts one horizontally-arranged smelting furnace which could be rotated, with oxygen lances at furnace bottom to blow enriched oxygen into the furnace for strengthened smelting. With enriched oxygen concentration of 73%, it could realize de facto autogenous smelting. There is no need for feeding coal, and when the smelter capacity is large enough, excessive heat from smelting can be used

902 

to treat some Cu oxides and low sulfur-containing gold concentrates after calcining and Ar-removal. This technology has been applied successfully at Vietnam Lao Cai Copper Smelter, Dongying Fangyuan Non-ferrous Metals Co., Ltd., Shandong Province, Shandong Humon Smelting Co., Ltd, Baotou Huading Copper Development Co., Ltd, Inner Mongolia, etc. among which, Dongying Fangyuan has reached 100,000t/a blister. Projects under designing and construction are Dongying Fangyuan Phase II designed to treat 1 million t/a multi-metal concentrates, reconstruction of Yuanqu Cu smelter of Norther Copper Co., Ltd designed to treat 500,000t/a multi-metal concentrates, Yuguang Au & Cu &Pb smelting waste treatment, Qinghai Copper 100,000t/a Cathode Cu Project, and Henan Zhongyuan Gold Smelter of Zhongjin Gold Corporation Limited designed to treat 1.5 million t/a complicated gold concentrates, etc. From post-commissioning operational experiences, bottom-blowing Cu smelting technology has demonstrated the following features as wide adaptability of feed, simple feed preparation, no-drying and pelletizing of concentrates, high enriched-oxygen concentration, low heat loss on furnace shell (no water cooling jacket on shell) , long lance life, easy operation, low dust rate, environmentally friendly, cost effective and high impurity removal efficiency, etc. In particular, enriched oxygen is blown directly to the matte layer, so no foaming slag will be formed, thus ensuring safety. Matte and slag separation in one furnace, without settling furnace, and Fe/SiO2 content is high as 1.6-2.0, with small slag quantity. Smelting slag and converting slag, after floatation, contains Cu<0.30%、Au<0.3g/t、 Ag<10g/t, and high Cu recovery rate (>98.5%), and Au/Ag recovery rate is also increased. Though smelting slag contain high Cu (2-4%)， Cu direct recovery rate is low, and quantity of slag returning to smelting is large (-10% of total concentrates),

since recycled slag is mixture of solid matte and slag, which will not participate in reaction in the smelting furnace and only need small amount of melting heat, total Cu recovery rate is high. If settling furnace is used, though Cu in slag is lowered and Cu direct recovery rate is increased,  in order to avoid furnace accretion, it is imperative to lower Fe/SiO2 content and increase slag quantity to produce discarded slag or be sent to floatation. In this regard, total Cu recovery rate is lowered, which is economically unreasonable. Bottom-blowing technology, as the representative technology for “Au/Ag Capturing from Matte”, has its unique advantage in treating Cu-bearing Au concentrates. Since it has no strict requirements on Cu content in concentrates, and the success of the process depends mainly on whether matte is produced, it could meet the demand of Au concentrates treatment to the maximum extent. 

### **Matte Converting** 

Matte converting technology is a little lagging behind. A majority of 85% matte uses converter for converting. PS converter is mature and reliable, electrolytic residual

anode can return to converter for treatment, with low energy consumption. Yet since converter operates discontinuously, off-gas volume fluctuates, air leakage at furnace openings is high, SO2 density in off-gas is low, and air leakage during ladle lifting and converter operation is high, therefore low altitude pollution can be caused and environmental conditions are bad. This is why there have been numerous researches and studies on continuous converting process to replace PS converter, such as flash converting, Ausmelt top-blowing submerged converting, Noranda converting, Mitsubishi converting and bottom-blowing converting, etc. 

### <u>Flash Converting</u> 

The first smelter adopting flash smelting and flash converting process (“Double Flash”) in the world is Kennecott Smelter in US, which was put into operation in 1995. The flash converting process it adopted was developed together by the smelter and OT, which produces Ca-Fe type slag with small amount of SiO2. The second one adopting the Double Flash process is Xiangguang Copper Co., Ltd, Shandong Province in China put into operation in 2007. There are two other smelters under construction, i.e., Tongling Non-ferrous Copper Technical Modification Project and Guangxi Jinchuan Non-ferrous Processing Project—400,000t/a Cu smelting. 

Except for Mitsubishi Continuous Cu Converting Process, the continuous converting process which is mature and could be used for large scale capacity is flash converting. Upon persistent improvement, Xiangguang Copper Co., Ltd which adopts flash converting developed Rotating Suspension Converting Technology. 

Flash converting process is that hot copper matte, after granulation or dry-type agglomeration, and drying with vertical mill, goes through continuous converting. Its advantages are that solid matte is easy t

o measure, converting process is easy to control, and also has high enriched oxygen concentration, low off-gas volume, cost effective offgas treatment, and high operationability. Yet it also lacks in the fact that the structure of flash converter and heat balance restricts it from treating cold materials like scraps, and requires an additional metallurgical furnace to melt scraps; moreover, the granulation of hot matte is a waste of energy, and the energy utilization is not economical. 

### - <u>Top blowing Submerged Converting Process</u> 

Zhongtiaoshan Houma Smelter is the first one in the world adopting Double TopBlowing, i.e., Ausmelt Top-blowing Smelting and Top-blowing Converting, and was put into operation in 1999. The second in China and the third in the world are Yunnan Tin

Group 100,000t/a Cu Smelter which was put into operation in 2012. Top-blowing converting process operates in batches, and is not a de facto continuous converting. Hot matte can be fed directly into the top-blowing converter or fed after granulation, or both. 

Top-blowing converter is identical to top-blowing smelting furnace, which has no settling zone which is not good for the separation of slag and Cu or matte; Cu in slag is high and could not realize continuous converting and separation in one single reactor; vertical structure makes it difficult to feed scraps, thus requiring an independent melting furnace. 

Oxygen is blown in the slag layer, so oxygen potential is high and slag type is SiFe type, which is easy to form foaming slag, therefore requires a lot of coal or coke as reductant. 

### <u>Noranda Converting Process</u> 

Noranda converting process uses ladles to transfer copper matte. Inside the furnace, except for gas phase, there are three phases, i.e., (semi) blister, white matte and slag. Air is blown continuously from side of the furnace in the white matte layer. Since slag is SiFe type, in order to avoid foaming slag, coke, cold materials and fluxes are fed together into the furnace. Though matte is not fed continuously, air blowing is continuous and offgas volume is stable, therefore could be regarded as continuous converting. Yet since there is white matte layer, S in blister is high as 1.2% and impurity content is high, before refining in anode furnace, blister shall be fed to converter for further converting and impurity removal. Air is blown with low pressure, and tuyere life is short (normally three months), so in order to prolong furnace life and improve operation efficiency, several sets of tuyeres are adopted to operate in turns. That is the main reason why Noranda Converting process has not become an advanced, mature and reliable continuous converting process and has not been widely applied. 

### <u>Mitsubishi Converting Process</u> 

Mitsubishi converting process can be categorized as top-blowing converting, yet different from Ausmelt top-blowing converting in the fact that Mitsubis

hi doesn’t apply submerged lance converting and lance sleeve is 0.3-0.8 m above bath level. It uses 10 or 9 lances, and the change of lances doesn’t affect each other. Its operation efficiency is high, and also since Mitsubishi furnace is large (diameter of Ф8-9m), bath is shallow (1m), and slag layer is thin (-0.1m), separation of matte and slag in one furnace could be realized. Two-phase operation, i.e. slag and blister phases, is adopted in Mitsubishi 

_Proceeding of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

905 

converting furnace and slag is Ca-Fe type (developed by Mitsubishi Materials Corporation), therefore slag has strong solubility of Fe3O4, and is less likely to form foaming slag, thus ensuring safety operation. Moreover, slag line has copper cooling jacket, so furnace life is longer. 

Mitsubishi continuous Cu smelting process adopts four launder-connected furnaces, i.e. one smelting furnace, one cleaning furnace, one converting furnace and two or three anode furnaces, which are arranged in descending elevations, and has strong comovement. This kind of arrangement requires precise process control. Since discarded slag is produced from smelting slag, which will be granulated to cool down similar like smelting slag. 

### <u>Enriched-oxygen bottom-blowing Converting Process</u> 

As the patent holder of bottom-blowing continuous converting technology, China ENFI Engineering Corporation, together with Yuguang Au&Pb Co., Ltd and Dongying Fangyuan Non-ferrous Metals Co., Ltd., conducted pilot plant test on continuous bottomblowing Cu matte converting process and uses cold (solid) matte to conduct continuous converting test. Slag is Si-Fe type. When uses two-phase operation, i.e., blister phase and slag phase, S in blister is 0.01-0.2%, and impurity content is low, which is between converter blister (0.01% S) and flash converter blister (1.2% S); when uses three-phase operation, i.e., blister phase, white matte phase and slag phase, S in blister is 0.7% and other impurity content is little higher, similar to Mitsubishi converter blister (0.7% S), and better than Noranda converter blister (1.2% S), that is because oxygen is blown from bottom-blowing converter bottom to oxidize blister. Industrial-scale test on continuous bottom-blowing converting of hot (liquid) matte was carried out in Dongying Fangyuan Non-ferrous Metals Co., Ltd, which testified the results from the pilot plant test and focused on testing Ca-Fe type slag. 

The success of the pilot plant test and industrial-scale test provides strong technical support for the following projects such as Yuguang Au&Pb 50,000-100,000t/a Cu smelting project, Fangyuan Non-ferrous Metals Co., Ltd Phase II 1 million t/a multimetal project and Henan Zhongyuan Gold Smelter of Zhongjin Gold Corporation Limited designed to treat 1.5 million t/a complicated gold concentrates which adopt the Double Continuous Bottom-blowing Process. 

Enriched-oxygen continuous bottom-blowing Cu smelting process has two proces

s routes: one is hot matte from smelting furnace flows directly to converting furnace; and 

_Proceeding of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

906 

the second is matte from smelting furnace, after cooling and granulation (granulation, dry-type pelletizing or crushing after cooling), is fed in solid form to converting furnace. 

These two process routes have their own advantages and disadvantages: 

If hot matte is fed, its sensible heat could be utilized, and when all the scraps are fed in the converting furnace at enriched oxygen concentration of 30%, autogenous smelting could be realized. Yet compared with the second process route of feeding cold (solid) matte, it produces more off-gas, and lower SO2 density, therefore, if elevate enriched oxygen concentration to treat copper scraps, off-gas volume will be largely decreased and SO2 density will be increased. By calculation, if enriched oxygen concentration is increased to 65%, it could treat scraps with same Cu metal amount, which is realistic since the dynamics of converting furnace is better than that of anode furnace and shaft furnace. In this way, sensible heat of hot matte can be fully utilized to treat scraps and decreases off-gas treatment cost. It testifies that continuous bottomblowing Cu smelting technology could not only treat Cu/Au concentrates, but also treat scraps with no additional fuels, thus proving it the ideal Cu smelting technology in the world. However, hot matte converting process has its deficiencies: 

1) Though the arrangement of one bottom-blowing smelting furnace, plus one or two bottom-blowing converting furnace, plus two rotary anode furnace in descending elevations has strong co-movement, it has bad cushioning capacity, and one furnace shutdown may affect the operation of other furnaces, thus lowering operation efficiency. 

2) Since smelting slag goes to floatation, and is not suitable for granulation. Smelting furnace is arranged in high elevation, which makes it hard to flow directly via launder to the ladles on ground level and needs cranes to lift ladles from high platforms. This poses operation risks.  If slag cleaning furnace is arranged, there is no need for ladle lifting with cranes, and the cleaning furnace could help to lower Cu in slag and increase Cu direct recovery rate. Yet, slag from cleaning furnace also needs to go to slag floatation, though the amount of reverted slag to smelting furnace is reduced. Moreover, with slag cleaning furnace, Fe/SiO2 ratio in slag is lower, slag amount is larger, total Cu recovery rate is lower, energy consumption is higher, thus operating cost is higher, which is to economical. 

3) If no craps is treated, enriched oxygen concentration is lower, air blowing is large, melt agitation is intense, and furnace campaign life is shortened. In order to have similar campaign life with smelting furnace, it is necessary to have a standby continuous converting furnace, yet this will increase capital cost and complicate building 

_

907 

arrangement. If a standby matte dry pelletizing system is adopted, one converting furnace is enough. 

If cold matte is fed in the converting furnace, smelting furnace and converting furnace operates independently. Since solid matte is easy to measure, converting furnace can be operated in a stable manner with little white matte layer formed, thus ensuring blister quality.  One bottom-blowing converting furnace and two rotary anode furnaces can be connected directly with launders. Smelting furnace can be arranged at a lower elevation and separate from the converting and anode furnaces, thus smelting slag ladle can be put on ground level, with simpler operation, and there is no need for a spare converting furnace. In this way, the plant building is simple, and capital cost is lower. When Cu in matte is 70%, enriched oxygen concentration is 75%, and when all craps are fed in converting furnace, autogenous operation can be realized.  1.2% coal needs to be added for slag reduction to avoid foaming slag to be formed. In this way, enriched oxygen concentration in converting furnace is high, air blowing volume is low, bath agitation is less intense, and have little impact on furnace lining, thus resulting in longer furnace life, less off gas volume, high SO2 density and lower operation cost for off gas handling. 

The calcium ferrite slag could lower the risk of foaming slag formation, yet is not suitable for processes which blow high-pressure air like the bottom-blowing converting process. The reason is that for bottom-blowing converting furnace, oxygen pressure in lances is high and energy produced is high, yet since calcium ferrite slag is less sticky and its flowability is better, the slag line is easily worn and furnace life is shortened. Therefore, it is better to use ferro-silicon slag. To be more conservative, three-phase operation is often used, i.e., slag phase, white matte phase and blister phase, from which blister quality is not as good, thus adding burden to anode furnace refining. If cold matte converting is adopted, since oxygen/feed ratio is easy to control, two-phase operation (slag phase and blister phase) can be controlled. 

In short, if no craps is treated, cold matte converting process is more feasible, safer and more reliable.

### **CONCLUSION** 

With stricter environmental restrictions and higher demand on clean production by smelters, environmentally friendly continuous copper smelting technology has become the trend for greenfield or brownfield copper and gold smelting projects, leaving little room for PS converter. 

In China, the commonly adopted continuous copper smelting technologies are Double Flash, Double Top-blowing, and Double Bottom-blowing. 

Double Top-blowing technology, due to its inherent restrictions, still has a long way to go to become a real continuous technology. 

Double Flash technology has its relati

ve advantage in treating high grade copper concentrate (22-27% Cu), and super-large smelter with single production line of 400,000t/a Cu. 

Double Bottom-blowing technology can treat various Cu (Au) concentrates (1227% Cu) with wide range of concentrate throughput (250,000 to 1.5 million t/a). Maximum single production line capacity is 300,000t/a Cu, and could reach to 400,000t/a Cu if scraps are treated in converting furnace. 

Continuous copper smelting technology can have different combination of processes based on feed, capacity and site conditions, such as bottom-blowing smelting plus flash converting, or fixed side-blowing smelting plus bottom-blowing converting. 

The selection of technology shall be based on the feed adaptability, feed preparation, capacity, environmental protection, energy consumption, capital cost, operation cost, furnace life, automation level and labor strength, and more importantly on Cu recovery rate. 

Since China relies greatly on importation of Cu (Au) concentrates, it is the permanent goal for smelters to decrease slag production and Cu in slag and increase Cu recovery rate in an economic way, and this is also the key for companies to add to their competitive strengths. Because of this, smelting slag floatation is the mainstream process for the time being, and it needs more researches and studies on arranging settling furnace (or other cleaning furnaces) to produce discarded slag, or delivering electric furnace slag for floatation, except in the case that Cu in discard slag from cleaning is the same or

lower than Cu in slag tailings, or as restricted by the site plan layout, there is not enough room for slag floatation system. 

Zero flux or fuel, and using self-melting slag for smelting is the goal for all metallurgists and the best way to reduce slag amount.  Feeding Au concentrates rather than limestone when there is a need for Fe/SiO2 adjustment, since Au concentrates contain higher SiO2 than Cu concentrates. It is also feasible to add gold-bearing quartz to smelt both Au and Cu and maximize economic returns. 

Advanced continuous Cu smelting process can not only produce stable offgas volume, but also produce high concentration SO2 off gas, which brings the application of new technologies, such as pre-conversion technology, and medium-low temperature heat recovery technology, etc. In order to meet the requirements on SO2 emission standards and total emission control, de-sulfurizing technologies with ionic liquid and active coke which could be recycled are adopted by smelters. 

In conclusion, with the joint effort of scientists and engineers in the Cu smelting industry, continuous Cu smelting technology will be further developed and improved. The pursuit of a simple, high-efficient, energy-conserving, safe and environmental technology will continue to be the development direction and target of Cu smelting technology.

### **ABSTRACT** 

Sulfurization and slow-cooling process was investigated for selective recovery of molybdenum (Mo) from the copper smelting slag. To get slag samples containing 0.5, 1.0 or 2.0 % of Mo, MoO3 reagent was added to a water cooled slag and heated at 1300 ºC for 1 hour in Ar atmosphere. After cooled and ground under 125  m, sample was mixed with FeS2 (pyrite) to be 7.5 or 15 of S/Mo molar ratio. This mixture was heated at 1300 ºC for 1 hour in Ar atmosphere and slowly cooled at 3 K/min. Characterization for these samples were performed by XRD, XRF, and SEM-EDS. A sulfide phase containing molybdenum, iron and sulfur was founded in 2.0 Mo wt.% slag, however, molybdenum was condensed in the magnetite phase in low grade molybdenum sample. 16.7 wt.% of Mo concentrate was obtained by flotation after ground under 125  m with PAX and MIBC at pH 6.6.

### **INTRODUCTION** 

A lot of hot melting slag has been produced worldwide in copper smelting. In Japan, approximately 2 million tons copper smelting slag is produced in a year [1]. There are also 7 copper smelters in Chile, of which annual slag production is larger than 4 million tons, and 45 million tons of slag is stocked in the country [2-3]. 

Copper concentrate contains many kinds of impurities [4]. Therefore, copper smelting slag sometimes contains both rare metals such as molybdenum, cobalt and nickel and base metals like iron, copper and zinc. Minimizing resource consumption and slag generation is a frequent topic of discussion worldwide that is especially important in Japan because of a shortage of slag utilization sites as well as a stable supply of resources [1]. Slag is used in cement production and as sandblasting grit, however, it is a problem that the amount of slag production is larger than it of slag consumption [1]. Therefore it is important to establish an economical recycling process to recover useful metals from the slag. 

In fact, numbers of methods for metal recovery or separation from copper smelting slag have been investigated [5]. Several investigations for molybdenum

recovery were also performed from the copper smelting slag or the other waste materials [6-10]. These methods are mainly based on hydrometallurgical or pyrometallurgical process. Usually, slag is rapidly cooled with water, which is called as water-granulation [10], and then it becomes poorly-crystalline structure substance. However, it is difficult **-** to recover selectively useful metals from the water cooled slag by physical separation because each useful element is poorly crystalline and not condensed in a specific phase. 

On the other hand, slag becomes crystalline substance and form many kinds of minerals if it had been slowly cooled [11]. In addition, the lower the cooling rate, the larger the mineral phases grow [12]. The objective of this study is to get molybdenum condensed phase which could be separate from the other phases. Generally, molybdenum sulfide such as MoS2, will be recovered by flotation. Therefore, in this study, slag was heated up and melted with small amount of pyrite, and slowly cooled to sulfurize molybdenum.

### **SUMMARY** 

The sulfurization of molybdenum was performed by pyrite addition, heating and slow cooling. We confirmed the formation of mixture of molybdenum sulfide and molybdenum-iron sulfide from the slag containing over 2% of Mo. On the other h

and, molybdenum was not sulfurized in low grade molybdenum slag. In this case, molybdenum would be distributed in magnetite phase. Moreover, other elements in the slag such as copper were also sulfurized by pyrite addition.

### **FEATURES OF THE BOTTOM BLOWN OXYGEN COPPER SMELTING TECHNOLOGY** 

Zhixiang Cui, Zhi Wang _Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd, Dongying City, China_

### **ABSTRACT** 

The first commercial scale bottom blown oxygen copper smelting furnace has been installed and operated at Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd. for 4 years. This is the first modern copper smelting technology developed in China with the advantages of: 

- 1) High oxygen enrichment, which results in high productivity, low off-gas volume and negative pressure inside the furnace; 

- 2) High Fe/SiO2 ratio in the slag, which not only reduce the direct cost of the flux (SiO2) but also reduce the slag volume and therefore the heat loss associated with the slag and workload of the slag cleaning; 

- 3) High grade matte (over 70 wt% Cu) and low Cu content (2-3 wt%) in the smelting slag which significantly increase the direct recovery of the smelting process; 

- 4) Autothermal operation. When normal concentrate is treated in the bottom blown oxygen furnace no extra fuel is required due to a) low temperature operation (11601180<sup>o</sup> C); b) less heat loss associated with slag and matte; c) high concentration oxygen reduces the heat loss associated with the off-gas; d) high heat efficiency as a result of submerge combustion.

### **INTRODUCTION** 

The major smelting technologies in modern copper making industry include flash smelting and bath smelting [1]. Ausmelt/Isasmelt using top blown and Noranda/Teniente using side blown are typical bath smelting technologies. In 1980s-1990s Hunan Shuikoshan Mineral Bureau, jointly with China Nonferrous Engineering and Research Institute (now China Enfi Engineering Corp.), developed the concepts of the bottom blown oxygen processes for both lead and copper smelting [2]. After the pilot test on 3000 ton copper per year scale in 1991, it was not progressed to industrial scope. 

Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd. was established in 1998 to produce electrolytic copper from scrap. It was in 2005 the company decided to expand its production capacity by introducing smelting-converting technology to produce blister copper from concentrate. The target was to find new technologies that could be applied to 1) treat low grade complex copper concentrate; 2) to recover not only copper but also other valuable metals such as gold and silver; 3) to produce off-gases with higher SO2 concentration for acid plant and 4) to have low operating costs while improving the environmental performance. 

After systematic investigations and comparisons the bottom blown oxygen technology was finally selected for copper smelting at Fangyuan company although there appeared to be risks to increase the scope from 3000 t/year directly to 100,000 t/year. The op

eration commenced on the end of 2008 and has been running for more than four years. Significant technical improvements have been achieved in areas such as oxygen lance design, feed preparation, off-gas handling, operating and process control strategies, refractory management, operator training and commissioning systems. This paper summaries the main features and operating experiences on the first commercial bottom blown oxygen copper smelting furnace in the World developed at Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd. 

### **FEATURES OF THE BOTTOM BLOWN OXYGEN TECHNOLOGY** 

Bottom blown oxygen smelting – PS rotary furnace converting – electrolysis refining is the process adopted at Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals for production of blister copper. The converting and refining technologies used at Fangyuan are similar to other copper plants. It is focused only on bottom blown oxygen smelting technology in this paper. 

### **Description of the Technology** 

Mixed feed materials with 7-10 wt% moisture are continuously transported by a belt conveyor into a high temperature melt in the furnace through the feed mouth located above the reaction zone. Oxygen and air are blown constantly by the oxygen lances into melting copper matte, in which iron and sulfur are rapidly oxidized and slag is also formed. Sulfur dioxide produced is directed through the waste-heat boiler and electric

precipitation, then led into the acid plant to produce sulfuric acid. Slag formed in the furnace can be tapped regularly through a taphole at the end of the furnace, lifted by a ladle to the slag site for slow cooling, followed by the flotation process to recover copper. Matte formed in the furnace is tapped regularly through a taphole on the middle part of the furnace, lifted by a ladle into the PS converter.

### **High Grade Matte and low Cu-containing slag** 

It can be seen from Table 1 that initially designed matte grade was 55 wt% Cu and the current matte grade has been increased to 75 wt% Cu. In the meantime the Cu content in the smelting slag is still 3 wt% which is much lower than most of other smelting slags corresponding to the same grade matte. This not only increases the direct recovery of copper in the smelting process but also decreases the weights of the matter and the following converting slag. It can be seen from Figure 6 that matte weight decreases with increasing matte grade. High grade matte can be produced in other smelting processes but they are usually associated with higher copper loss in the slag. [5] The bottom-blown furnace at Fangyuan produces high grade matte and low Cu slag simultaneously. Understanding of this advantage requires further fundamental studies. 

### **Autothermal Operation** 

It can be seen from Table 1 that 2.46 t/h coal was suggested in the bottom-blown furnace according to the initial design. In the current operation it is not necessary to add coal in smelting of normal copper concentrate. This means that autothermal operation has been achieved in the bottom blown furnace at Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals. This not only reduces energy consumption but also significantly decreases CO2 emission. It was the combination of the unique design of the bottom blown furnace and optimum operating parameters enabling the process to be autogenous smelting. 

The possible reasons for autogenous smelting include 1) solid-containing slag can be smoothly tapped from the furnace enabling the furnace to be operated at relatively lower temperature which requires less energy; 2) high Fe/SiO2 ratio in slag results in low slag volume and therefore less heat loss; 3) high matte grade results in low matte volume and therefore less heat loss 4) high oxygen enrichment reduces the heat loss associated with the off-gas; 5) most of the oxidization reactions involving oxygen occur in the bottom part of the furnace. The heat generated from these reactions can be efficiently absorbed by the matte and slag which has been described in details as a submerged combustion reactor. [6-7].

### **CONCLUSIONS** 

Over four years operation at Dongying Fangyuan Nonferrous Metals, the bottom blown copper smelting furnace has shown great potentials. Continuous improvements have been made in the first commercial bottom blown copper smelting furnace in the World. The important features associated with the bottom blown copper smelting technology at Fangyuan have been discussed. Some of the features are unique to the operation at Fangyuan and cannot be explained by the conventional metallurgical theories. Systematic fundamental studies are required to fully understand the advantages of the bottom blown copper smelting technology and further improve the operations.

### <u>Weak Acid Treatment—Gas-Liquid Separation Technology</u> 

All the off gases produced at copper smelting process, a weak sulfuric acid is produced, called waste acid in smelting industry, with fluorine, chlorine, arsenic and heavy metal impurities, leading to resource waste and environmental pollution. The conventional processing is the neutralization process which produces high volume of inferior gypsum, high gypsum stock and large space to storage and may result in secondary pollution of water; the traditional process produces neutralized waste water, and it is a burden of sewage emission of smelter complex. 

The new concentration and recovery technology independently developed by DF, it make use of the surplus heat of the contact process in the acid plant, removing the impurities by a concentration of impurities’ compose. With this process it can produce a

kind of acid solution that is clean enough to be added into acid system of the acid plant to produce commercial acid. It features with simple flow, small footprint and low operational cost, while it stands out mainly because it can recover sulfur without harming the environment, promising a huge economic and social benefit. 

At present DF can increase the weak acid from 15% of H2SO4 to 60% of H2SO4. The sulfuric acid loss is not more than 5%.  The extraction rate of fluorine and chlorine are 80% and 90% respectively; arsenic loss is less than 5%. The sulfuric acid we produce meets the superior level standard of GB/T534-2002. The new process avoids the use of lime or limestone to neutralize the weak acid, and consequently it won’t produce a paste of gypsum neither waste water. ### <u>Dust treatment and Comprehensive Recovery of The Precious Elements</u> 

Since 1950s, in China, many Copper Smelters, research centers and design institutes have been studying about the copper converter dust and certain progress has been achieved. But so far there is not a ideal technology as the dust ingredients are changing. The current operational processes to treat converting dust are shown below: 

- Dust →Reducing Smelting (Blast Fce) →Pb/Bi Alloy Electrolysis →Bi Pyro-refining; 

- Dust →Leaching →Extracting →Replacement →Crystallization; [12]  Dust →Water Immersion →Reducing Smelting of Leaching Slag. 

DF consulted to much relevant documents<sup>[10-11]</sup> and it did lots of tests. DF have developed a technology to comprehensively recover valuable metals such as copper (Cu), lead (Pb), zinc (Zn), cadmium (Cd), bismuth (Bi) and arsenic (As) according to the dust characterist

ics and the physical and chemical properties of the elements. The new technology processing bases in  the fact that there are differences between the physical and chemical properties of the elements, and it combines hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy methods together. The process has two times of continuous acid leaching, it dissolves copper, zinc, cadmium and arsenic (Cu/Zn/Cd/As) into the solution, after which; arsenic (As) will be treated separately. Then successively: Cu, copper is recovered as blister copper or black copper; Zn, zinc as monohydrate zinc sulfate; Cd, cadmium as fine cadmium, while; Pb/Bi/Au/Ag, lead, bismuth, gold and silver remain in the leached slag. Then in the pyro part, through smelting, electrolysis and refining, the elements in the leached slag will be effectively separated to produce electrolysis lead (Pb), fine bismuth (Bi) and silver-zinc slag (Ag/Zn slag). This is circulating coming back, returning to precious metals smelting workshop.

### **CONCLUSIONS** 

Through the cooperation of university and long-term research, the BBS process in DF has had a continuous improvement and progress characterized in lower and lower energy consumption. The operational indexes reach the most advance level internationally. 

Meantime the associated technologies, complementary and ancilliary are completing and impulsing the BBS technology. Nowadays we can not only produce high quality cathode of copper, but also guarantee the recovery of the valuable metal plus almost zero emission, showing a strong competiveness under the force of stricter and hard environmental regulations. 

Bottom Blown Oxygen Smelting technology (BBS) is in its fourth generation of smelting technology, which in short period has showed unusual advantages from BBS1 to BBS4. The new orientation of BBS technology shall be the new step of a "Continuous Copper Smelting" technology (CCS). We believe that the combination of DF's technologies "BBS and CCS" will bring a new future to copper smelting industry.

### **INTRODUCTION** 

The reduction furnace is integrated in the copper recovery line, its main task being the reduction of oxides contained in the slag discontinuously tapped from El Teniente con

verter through viscosity adjustment by the addition of coke. Additionally, solids are smelted as reverts that come from other process stages to recover the copper contained in that material. The furnace properties allow the smelting of seed matte to start up the smelter in case of total shutdown or metal storage in case of general repairs. The reducing agent for copper oxides, magnetite, and other oxides is coke which is added through the roof while a reducing atmosphere is maintained on the slag bath. Both the coke and reverts are fed through feed openings with the help of hoppers located in the primitive circle of electrodes. Hoppers are loaded with a mobile feeder, equipped with a hopper and a vibration system, responsible for conveying process material to the furnace. The material is partially mixed in the hoppers by alternating the materials loaded. Coke reduces the magnetite contained in TC slag releasing the metal particles trapped thus facilitating its coalescence. Once the reduction process is completed, the sedimentation stage starts where metal particles settle and generate a higher density phase, matte. The slag with 0.8% of copper content is evacuated through two tap holes located on the west side of the EF and loaded into rail cars with the help of 9-ton ladles; next it is conveyed to its final destination in the north area of the smelter. During the process, carbon monoxide and other volatile substances are produced, such as sulfur dioxide, hydrogen, and gaseous metals; for example, zinc smoke gas. A slight negative pressure facilitates the entry of air from the outside whose volume will depend on the amo

unt of gas produced during the process. This outer air coming in from the wall openings and the furnace roof promotes burning of carbon monoxide, a process where gas temperature can reach as high as 1200°C. Smoke gases containing a certain amount of dust are evacuated through an opening on the dome and then pass through an electrostatic precipitator that collects the dust and the gas is released into the atmosphere. ### **ABSTRACT** 

Continuous converting of copper matte or white metal into blister copper can be carried out in a new high - intensity molten layer reactor that operates with dry, -65 mesh grinded matte or white metal and technical oxygen.  The reactor operates at 1500-1600ºC producing a blister copper with 0.5 – 0.8%S which can be refined in conventional form, and a slag with less than 8% Cu.  The reactor operates continuously with no fugitive emissions, generating and off gases with over 50% SO2. The phenomenological model of the molten – layer reactor can predict with good agreement the results obtained in a pilot prototype reactor. 

_Proceeding of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_

### **DESCRIPTION OF THE MOLTEN – LAYER REACTOR** 

In this new concept of reactor for copper converting<sup>1,2</sup> , instead of forming a reacting flame like in a flash converter or a reacting bath such as the Isasmelt or conventional Peirce – Smith converters, all reaction takes place in a molten layer flowing by gravity along the inner reactor’s walls, which allows a reaction time of 20 to 30 s of the molten phase with the gaseous atmosphere, reaching the equilibrium conditions before the metal is separated from the slag in the lower settler. 

The surface of the molten layer reacts intensely with the oxygen of the gas phase generating SO2 and a large amount of heat, which is removed both in the off gases and through the water – cooled walls of the reactor. 

In Figure 1 is shown a schematic representation of the main physico – chemical phenomena that takes place along the flowing molten emulsion of metal – sulphides – slag and gases. 



Figure 1–  Schematic representation of the physico-chemical phenomena taking place on a molten – layer reactor wall 

The physico – chemistry of copper matte convertion to blister copper is well understood, and can be found elsewhere<sup>3</sup> .  The secuential oxidation of the iron to wustite and further neutralization to fayalite is followed by the oxidation of copper sulphide to cuprous oxide and its simultaneous reduction with copper sulphide to metallic copper (blister) according to:

All of these reactions are exothermic, with a total heat release for a typical copper white metal of 72% Cu of - 83,500 Kcal/ton. 

### **KINETICS, HEAT GENERATED AND REMOVED IN THE REACTOR** 

For this type of reactor, the high speed of the gas-solid jet emerging from the matte-oxygen burners (40-50 m/s)  precludes the formation of a flame, since clouds of copper and iron sulphides and oxygen have a flame propagation velocity of only 2 to 5 cm/s<sup>4</sup> therefore, all reactions should takes place along the flowing molten layer formed

over the walls of the reactor, rather than in a flame emerging from the tangential burners, as it has been assumed occurs in cyclonic reactors5 . The time that takes a 35 microns copper matte particle to reach 1200ºC under the intense thermal radiation prevailing inside the reactor can be estimated by the equation: Assuming an initial temperature of the particles of 20ºC and a molten layer and gases temperature of 1600ºC, the time required for the particle to reach 1200ºC is 0.1 s, time span 15 times larger than the time spent by the particle in the emerging jet of solid and oxygen before it reaches the molten layer which is about 6x10-3 s, conditions that precludes any reaction of the solids in the jet. Since the reactors walls have water cooled jackets, a solid layer of blister copper – magnetite form over them, which protects the reactor from erosion and corrosion. ### **ABSTRACT** 

In the present paper, the development of the partial roasting technology for Mina Ministro Hales (MMH) copper concentrate containing arsenic is described. The work on enargite-rich copper concentrates started with small scale tests in a rotary furnace at Boliden Ronnskar, Sweden, followed by pilot plant tests with actual MMH concentrate both at Boliden Ronnskar and at Universidad de Concepciуn, Chile.  The results from the test work showed that it was possible to produce calcine with less than 0.3% Arsenic (As) by partial roasting in a fluidized bed at temperatures that avoid bed sintering, while at the same time maintain a residual sulphur of 20%.  This know-how was subsequently used for the design of the full-scale MMH concentrate roaster outside Calama, Chile. The Boliden knowhow is now part of the Outotec roasting technology.

### **INTRODUCTION** 

Partial roasting prepares copper sulphide concentrates for subsequent pyrometallurgical operations. The purpose of roasting is to remove as much as possible of impurity elements like arsenic and antimony while maintaining a maximum of sulphur content in the calcine. The sulphur is needed in the subsequent matte smelting process as fuel and to form a matte.  [1]. 

Partial roasting of copper concentrates is accomplished by controlling the amount of air to the concentrate; a predetermined amount of sulphur is removed, and only part of the iron sulphide is oxidized to magnetite. This ensures an efficient removal of arsenic as volatilized oxide and sulphide As-compounds. The control of the oxygen potential to magnetite formation of iron is essential, since operation with more oxidizing conditions will result in massive formation of ferric iron, i.e. hematite, which must be avoided. It is commonly reported that oxidizing conditions during roasting will reduce the arsenic removal efficiency due to reactions between ferric iron and arsenic oxide, which will form stable non-volatile iron-arsenate. 

The arsenic removal is very much depending of both the mineralogy of the arsenic rich minerals and the presence of minerals that could re

act with arsenic fume and form non-volatile arsenic compounds. Pure arsenic-rich copper minerals like enargite (Cu3AsS4) and tennantite (Cu12As4S13) contains on a stoichiometric basis about 20% As, but in a commercial concentrate the As-content will vary according to the proportions of the different constituting minerals such as pyrite, chalcopyrite, chalcocite, enargite, tennantite etc.  Roasting of commercial arsenic-containing copper concentrates will normally result in calcine with a residual arsenic content less than 0.3 %, which normally is an acceptable level in a feed to a copper smelter.[1]. 

The new MMH mine close to Calama will produce a typical example of an enargite containing copper concentrate. Other main minerals in the MMH copper concentrate are pyrite, chalcocite and inert compounds. 

Copper concentrates with similar mineralogical constituents has been present in other copper concentrates that was treated by partial roasting at the Boliden Ronnskar smelter in the past. The knowledge and test work performed at Boliden in the past is a part of the knowhow for developing the MMH roasting process. The Boliden knowhow is now part of the Outotec roasting technology. The other contributor to the knowledge of how to treat the MMH concentrate is Codelco in cooperation with the University of Conception. 

The present paper covers the development of partial roasting of enargite concentrates starting with the work made at Boliden in the early 1980´s up to the tests at University of Concepciуn that entirely are focused on the MMH concentrate. The paper also describes the general outline of the MMH roaster as it has being built.

### **ROASTING TESTS OF ENARGITE AT BOLIDEN** 

The Boliden copper smelter has a very long history of treating arsenic containing concentrates. The technology was for 50 years based on multiple hearth roasters, but they were taken out of operation and replaced by a fluidized bed roaster in the early 1980´s. The change in roasting technology made it necessary to better understand how e.g. enargite containing copper concentrates best should be processed to maximize the arsenic removal. The test work was initially made by small scale laboratory tests and subsequently by larger pilot plant tests [2]. 

These tests are relevant for the MMH project since the tested concentrates had a similar mineralogical constituency as the MMH concentrate, i.e. the same minerals but in different proportions. 

The minimum roasting temperature was initially set by TGA tests. They clearly showed that a temperature of more than 620 °C was necessary to obtain a significant arsenic removal. 

The laboratory roasting tests were made in an electrically heated rotary furnace, Figure 1, with batches of 50 gram. The focus was on studying the roasting result as function of temperature, time and mineralogical composition. The roasting temperature varied between 550 °C and 850 °C while the roasti

ng time ranged from 5 to 60 minutes. The standard test material contained about 8% As (as enargite and some tennantite), 22 % Cu, 20% Fe (mainly as pyrite) and 33% S.

### **SULPHATION ROASTING OF AN ENARGITE CONCENTRATE** 

B.  Chambers, C.  Pickles and J. Peacey _Robert M. Buchan Department of Mining Queen’s University Kingston, Ontario Canada K7L 3N6 John.Peacey@queensu.ca_ 

### **ABSTRACT** 

Due to the increasing difficulty of finding conventional copper and gold ore bodies, the processing of complex ores, such as those containing enargite, is being explored.  A sulphation roast, weak-acid leach, electrowinning process flowsheet was studied as a possible new treatment method for copper concentrates containing significant amounts of enargite. The sulphation roasting of an enargite concentrate was investigated in the laboratory in order to determine the behaviour of arsenic as a function of roasting conditions. Diagnostic leaching tests were then used to estimate the probable arsenic, copper and iron phases in the resulting calcine. Based on the estimated heat and mass balances, the economics of a sulphation roast-leach-electrowinning process was compared to that for the conventional partial dearsenizing roast and sale of calcine to copper smelters. 

_Proceeding of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

980 

### **INTRODUCTION** 

Enargite is a complex copper-arsenic sulfide (Cu3AsS4) mineral, typically containing significant gold values. However, the world’s copper smelters have a limited capacity for processing high-arsenic copper concentrates and the treatment and disposal of the resulting arsenic-containing effluents is both expensive and environmentally challenging.  Large copper deposits containing significant amounts of enargite are found particularly in Chile as well as other countries, and the increasing demand for copper and gold has spurred research into developing more effective methods of extracting valuable metals from enargite concentrates. This paper presents the results of laboratory research [1] on the sulphation roasting of an enargite concentrate and diagnostic leaching tests of the resulting calcines, as well as a preliminary economic comparison with a conventional partial roast and sale of the low-arsenic calcine. 

A thermodynamic analysis based on a proposed reaction mechanism for the sulphation roasting of an enargite concentrate, using HSC Chemistry® 6.1, was detailed in a recent paper [2] in order to develop an operating window and assess the overall potential feasibility of the proposed flowsheet. This analysis showed that at temperatures between about 500 to 700<sup>o</sup> C, copper arsenate and minor amounts of iron arsenate coexist, but above about 700<sup>o</sup> C copper arsenate is the dominant species. At low gas/solid ratios arsenic can be removed through volatilization, while at high gas/solid ratios, arsenic is retained in the calcine. A previous paper by Peacey [3], reviewed the current status of roasting and hydrometallurgical processes for treating enargite concentrates. Based on preliminary test work results, the relative proje

ct economics of the various processes, for treating an enargite concentrate from Kinross’s Mantos del Oro deposit in Chile, were compared. It was concluded that partial roasting is the only commercially proven option offering the lowest project risk as well as much more attractive economics than the hydrometallurgical options evaluated. 

The sulphation roasting of secondary copper concentrates containing cobalt values has commercially operated in Zambia and Zaire since the 1950’s. Guntner [4] recently reviewed the sulphating roasting of copper-cobalt concentrates. Also, sulphation roasting of chalcopyrite concentrates operated commercially at the Lakeshore mine in Arizona in the 1970’s [5]. Published papers on the sulphation roasting of enargite concentrates, however, could not be found, suggesting that this subject has not been investigated experimentally. 

### **EXPERIMENTAL** 

The enargite concentrate used in this research was from a deposit at Kinross’s La Coipa Mine in Chile with a composition of 24.6% Cu, 5.7% As, 18.0% Fe, 35.1% S and 21 g/t Au. Mineralogical analysis showed the presence of mainly enargite (30%), pyrite (40%), covellite (14%) and silica (16%). 

_Proceeding of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

981 

Bench-scale static-bed roasting tests were performed in order to investigate the behavior of an enargite concentrate under sulphation roasting conditions as a function of temperature and gas composition (O2 and SO2). Simultaneous thermogravimetric and differential thermal analysis coupled with evolved gas analysis (TG/DTA w/EGA) was also employed to investigate the chemical reactions occurring during the heating of the enargite concentrate in air. Diagnostic shake flask leaching tests were utilized to determine the solubility of copper, iron and arsenic in the static bed roast products as a means of inferring the probable major mineral phases. 

Figure 1 depicts the bench scale experimental equipment that was utilized to perform all of the static bed roasting work. Samples were loaded into a quartz sample carrier and allowed to react for a designated retention time. The bed thickness was minimized to reduce any diffusion or mass transfer limitations. The reaction atmosphere was controlled by varying the flowrates of nitrogen, oxygen and sulphur dioxide in the inlet gas using a constant total flowrate of 600 mL/min. 



















Figure 1- Schematic diagram of the static bed tube furnace. 

Diagnostic leach tests were performed in 125 mL shake flasks containing 50 mL of leaching solution and approximately 0.5 g of sample. Calcine samples were agitated at 300 rpm at a constant temperature of 80<sup>o</sup> C. Samples were sequentially leached in distilled water, 10 g/L sulphuric acid, and finally in a 50 g/L sulphuric acid solution, for 12 hours. The solution samples from each leach period were analyzed for Cu, Fe and As using ICP and the final leached residue was digested in aqua regia for ICP analysis.

These results suggest that it should be possible to carry out a sulphation roast of an enargite concentrate at a temperature of about 550<sup>o</sup> C to yield a calcine containing up to 90% of the initial arsenic as copper arsenate. This calcine should be readily leachable under acidic conditions to achieve high copper recovery while extracting sufficient ferric ion into solution to allow precipitation of a stable ferric arsenate or scorodite precipitate.

A sulphation roast/leach, although proven for copper/cobalt concentrates would still be a new process and therefore represents a much higher level of project risk than the partial roast option. Cyanidation of the acid leach residue should be able to achieve high gold recoveries but further test work w

ould be required to prove this. A sulphation roasting/leach/SX/EW flowsheet for treating enargite concentrates should be technically feasible and able to achieve high copper and gold recoveries as well as precipitation of arsenic as scorodite. ### Songlin Zhou

### **ABSTRACT** 

This paper introduces the principle of rotation-suspension copper smelting process, feature of pulse cyclone burner and their production application. Professor Songlin Zhou of Xiangguang Copper puts forward a reaction mechanism of particle collision for smelting intensification and develops rotation-suspension copper smelting process and pulse cyclone burner on the basis of this mechanism, and has successfully applied to smelting and converting furnaces in Xiangguang Copper. Four years practice indicates: pulse cyclone burner has some advantages-big production capacity, complete reaction, stable furnace running, high availability, low flue dust, high thermal load, less wear of reaction shaft wall and etc. Thanks to these advantages, maximum feed volume is 400t/h, availability rate is 98%, flue dust rate is 4% and thermal load is 3000 MJ/m<sup>3</sup> .h.

### **1. INTRODUCTION** 

Suspension smelting is a high-efficiency space smelting process whose main representatives are flash smelting methods of Outokumpu Finland and Inco Canada. The burner is a core equipment to realize suspension smelting. The CJD (Central Je

t Distributor) burner is the main unit which has more applications at present. It is developing towards super-strengthening smelting direction as a modern copper smelter, flash suspension smelting and CJD burner face tough challenge, for example: insufficient reaction, high raw-material rate, furnace condition fluctuation, high copper content in slag, high flue dust rate, severe boiler accretion and serious wear to reaction shaft which limit capacity increasing and sustainable development of flash suspension smelting. 

Therefore, Professor Sonlin Zhou of Xiangguang Copper, leading experts group carried out numerous theories research and industrial test to put forward “particle collision” reacting principle which can realize strengthening smelting. Based on this principle, they invent rotation-suspension smelting process<sup>[1]</sup> and the pulse cyclone burner<sup>[2]</sup> (PC burner). 

In May 2009 Xiangguang has changed that old CJD concentrate burner on FSF to PC concentrate burner. In April, 2011, Xiangguang has changed that old CJD matt burner on FCF to PC matt burner. After four years operation, it shows that the new burners have a lot of advantages like as large production capacity, complete reaction, stable furnace condition, high operation rate, lower flue dust rate, low copper content in slag, high heat load and a little wear for reaction shaft wall. The maximum charging amount reaches to 400t/h, 98% availability, 4% flue dust rate and 3000 MJ/m<sup>3</sup> .h heat load in FSF. 

### **2. ROTATION-SUSPENSION SMELTING PROCESS AND PULSE CYCLONE BURNER** 

### **Research for Reaction Principle of Particle Collision** 

After a long-term investigation and research, it is found that the main reasons of insufficient reaction, bad condition of the furnace, high flue dust rate and severe wall to reaction shaft are as follows: Ⅰ, influenced by different material behavior, different particle size and different combustion temperature and uneven mixture of gas and particle, the reaction speed of material particle entering reaction shaft is not same which makes small and flammable particles get prior reaction to make oxygen consume as peroxide while bigger and nonflammable particles react slowly to less oxidize state; Ⅱ, the effect of material distribution is not good during large charging. The distributing air is easy to 

_Proceedings of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

997 

make oxygen and particles uneven and bad mixture; Ⅲ, because umbrella-shaped particles in reaction shaft is suspending to free fall down and have less chance to collide between particles, the opportunity is small for peroxidizing and less oxidizing particles to rereaction and polymerization which would result in insufficient reaction and high flue dust rate etc. This proves that flash smelting only consider primary reaction state of particles in reaction shaft, but not take whole process into consideration as particles stay in reaction shaft, so it is difficult to realize s

uper-strengthening smelting. 

Therefore, Xiangguang copper proposes a reaction principle called particle pulsation collision model to realize super-strengthening smelting on basis of abundant theories research and industrial tests. Its main points are as follows referring to Figure 1: (1) small and flammable particles react priority to become peroxide; (2) oxygen diffusion speed inside bigger particle is lower than interior consumption speed, so bigger particles inside is less-oxidizing and form reacting burble while outside is continuing from oxidize to peroxide. The bigger particle will explode to lots of small particles under rising temperature and reacting burble force; (3) followed oxidizing reaction, oxygen in gas phase runs out to produce zero pressure of oxygen partial in gas phase under 2 meters of reaction shaft top. The new particles is far from presumed oxidation degree to be owe-oxidation or non-oxidation; (4) during falling process, particles collide with each other to grow up, so peroxidizing particles get reduction by less-oxidation ones; (5) upper part of reaction shaft mainly occur reactions between oxygen and particles as lower part mainly happen collision and reactions among particles. Particle collision is the basic way to transmit oxygen.

### **Features of Rotation-Suspension Smelting Process** 

On the base of particle collision, Xiangguang develops super-strengthening rotation-suspension copper smelting process which main features are collision reaction, cyclone, pulse and the air channel is inside and materials are outside. 

### <u>(1) Adopting the principle of particle collision to ensure full reaction</u> 

The smelting process inside reaction shaft is divided into two parts by rotationsuspension. The first part (upper part of reaction shaft) is to strengthen reactions between oxygen and particles, taking smelting as a example, the main reaction are 2CuFeS2+O2=2FeS+Cu2S+SO2 ； 2FeS+3O2 =2FeO+2SO2 ； 6FeO+O2 =2Fe3O4 ； 2Cu2S+3O2 =2Cu2O+ 2SO2. The second part (lower part of reaction shaft) is to intensify reactions among particles, taking smelting as a example, the main reaction is FeS+ 3Fe3O4 (peroxide）=10FeO+SO2 ；2CuFeS2 + 2Fe3O4 （peroxide）=Cu2S+2FeS+6FeO+SO2 ； 

_Proceedings of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

999 

Cu2O（peroxide）+ FeS =FeO+ Cu2S ; 2FeO+SiO2 =Fe2SiO4. 

The principle of particle collision guarantees sufficient reaction in the space smelting process and solve a series of problems existing in the flash smelting. 

<u>(2) Intensifying mixture and collision of oxygen and particles by dispersing material in a cyclone way</u> 

For the flash smelting, the particles in umbrella-shaped suspension are distributed in the whole reaction shaft, see Figure 2. And in this condition, there are three problems. The first one is that, when there is a large charging amount, the horizontal momentum of distributi

on air is smaller than the vertical momentum of material and thus it is hard for particles to disperse. Most of particles get together in the middle section, resulting in a bad mixture of oxygen and particles; the second one is that, as the particles fall freely in a state of suspension, there is a slim chance for peroxide particles and less oxidizing particles to collide and react, resulting in an incomplete reaction, unreacted material and a high flue dust rate; the third one is that, the whole reaction shaft is full of the high-temperature particles, which would cause the severe erosion to the shaft wall and thus a short lifetime, and cause also a heavy heat loss and a high energy consumption. 

The cyclone, a swirling flow in a high-speed revolution, has a strong diffusivity and entrainment ability in nature. Rotation-suspension smelting process exactly adopts the way of formation of cyclone and generates a swirling flow in a form of inverted cyclone in the reaction shaft. As it is showed by Figure 3, the particles, in a state of swirling flow and in a form of inverted cyclone, are distributed in the center of reaction shaft. This kind of process has the following advantages: (1)the strong diffusivity and entrainment ability of the swirling flow will bring a good mixture of oxygen and particles; (2)in the swirling flow, the prolonged reaction path and reaction time, as well as the different movement directions and speeds will bring more chance for the particles in rotating fluid to collide and react, thus contributing to a complete reaction, no unreacted materials, de-impurity effect and a low flue dust rate;(3) as the particles react in the center of the shaft, there will be no erosion to the shaft wall and a low heat loss makes the pyritic smelting is possible for saving energy.

### <u>(3) Intensifying the pulse collision by adding the central pulse oxygen</u> 

The central oxygen for the pulse is added in the center of the cyclone swirling flow. The central oxygen occupies 5% of the total oxygen which is necessary for reaction. In the pulse swirling flow, when the central oxygen quantity led into the pulse is more than the entrainment ability, the central oxygen will cause expansion, producing an outward acceleration in radial direction. When the central oxygen is stopped leading into the pulse, the entrainment in inner side will cause negative pressure, producing an inward acceleration in radial direction. This process is periodically repeated, which causes the airflow pulsation in radial direction. The pulse airflow can change the movement behavior of particles and enable the particles to produce the pulse acceleration and move in a reciprocating way in radial direction, bringing about the pulse collision, heat and mass transfer and reaction among parti

cles. 

_Proceedings of Copper 2013 Santiago, Chile_ 

1001 

<u>(4) Intensifying the heat and mass transfer and reaction efficiency by feeding in a way of</u> “the air channel is inside and materials are outside” 

The feeding way of flash smelting is “the air channel is outside and materials are inside”, that is, materials are inside of the process air channel. The feeding way of Rotationsuspension smelting process is “the air channel is inside and Materials are Outside”, that is, materials are outside of the air channel. This kind of feeding way has the following merits: the contacting area for particle swarm and process air(oxygen) is increased and thus the heat and mass transfer and reaction efficiency are intensified; without the air curtain effect of process air on particle swarm, the materials can have a direct contact with the high-temperature regurgitant flue gas caused by swirling flow and thus the temperature is increased rapidly, which makes it easy to reach to the fire point and speeds up the chemical reaction. 

### **Pulse Cyclone Burner** 

Xiangguang developed PC burner based on the features of the Rotation-suspension technology via the computer simulation studies as well as a large number of industrial tests, The structure of PC burner includes a channel for materials, a channel of process air, a pulse oxygen channel or a fuel channel. See Figure 4. 

The structure and working principle of PC burner are very different from those of CJD burner, such as the former has no jet distributor and air regulator, etc. Its working principle is: the process air rotates into the furnace at a high speed of 100-200m/s and generates a flow distribution in the form of inverted cyclone. After a free fall outside of the process air channel, the material particles are entrained by the cyclone to have a mixture. And then the central pulse oxygen is led into the cyclone swirling flow, with the pulse oxygen occupied 5% of the process oxygen. The process air, materials and pulse oxygen form a gas-solid mixing flow which rotates and pulse at a high-speed in the reaction shaft and the heat and mass transfer, oxidation combustion, collision and coalescence, smelting or converting reaction are all achieved in this flow.

### **ABSTRACT** 

It has been more than 10 years since the reported discovery of a novel technology, using molten calcium/sodium sulphates/arsenates salts for the removal of Arsenic from blister copper. The published data showed that using appropriate flux proportions, 90% arsenic elimination could be obtained while minimising slag production. A slag containing a very high arsenic concentration was produced with a marginal copper solubility and a low vapour pressure for arsenic gaseous species. The path used for the development of this technology, from the fundamental work to plant trials is re-assessed in this paper. Based on the published data, advanced thermodynamic models are used in the present paper to generate process maps, showing the impact of slag composition and the oxygen content in copper on equilibrium level of arsenic in firerefined copper. The best conditions for refining blister copper using the sulphate flux to produce a finished copper charge, having the required levels of arsenic to meet electrorefinery requirements, are outlined in the paper. The advantages and disadvantages of the use of these molten slats are discussed in the paper. With stricter environmental
