### **INTRODUCTION** 

In the primary lead smelting process in the blast furnace or at the decopperizing stage in an electric furnace, a copper/lead speiss is generated under a strongly reductive smelting operation as a final by-product, which contains considerable amounts of lead and impurities such as arsenic. This speiss is usually directed to copper smelting companies for metal recovery since primary lead smelting plants do not possess this product [1]. The copper/lead speiss constrains between 40-60 wt% Cu and 15-25 wt% Pb, depending on various factors such as the lead smelting process and composition of the raw base material [2]. 

The recovery of valuable elements and the stabilization of the heavy metals contained are the major concern in the treatment of speiss. Previous research work has been carried out on the phase relations, activities and minor element distribution for the Fe-Pb-As [3] and  FeCu-As [4] systems saturated with carbon at 1473K. However, the high content of lead and copper in this type of reductive materials plays an important role on the recovery of the metals. For this reason it is necessary to study the Cu-Fe-Pb-As system, considering lead, copper and iron as mayor components in order to clarify its behavior. 

Hence it is important to study the phase relations and distribution of minor elements in the Cu-Fe-Pb-As system saturated with carbon. The study of this system will also provide the fundamental information on a new proposed process at laboratory scale to eliminate arsenic from the arsenic-rich copper/lead speiss generated during the primary lead smelting in the blast furnace or from the by-product produced during the decopperizing stage in the electric furnace. 

The present research study revealed that three condensed and immiscible phases of lead-rich, copper-rich and iron-rich coexist during the equilibrium at 1473K and by using its separation, arsenic might be concentrated and eliminated into the less valuable iron-rich alloy phase, while precious metals of silver, gold and platinum can be recovered into the valuable copper-rich and lead-rich alloy phases. The modeling considers parameters such as sulfur concentration in copper, packed bed geometry, diffusivity and kinetics parameters, etc., and will be developed and simulated by using the software COMSOL Multiphysics. It is expected that the modeling will be able to describe and predict the behavior at a labora

### **CONCLUSIONS** 

It is possible to notice the direct dependence of the sulfur final concentration respect to the oxygen concentration present in the injected air to the reactor. This may be explained by the increased formation of SO2 by having more oxygen available. 

Also, another important parameter is the matte area versus reaction perimeter ratio, which changes with respect to the packed bed arrangement and conditioning the good performance of the system. 

On the other hand, it must be taken into account that the discretization mesh used by the software at the time of simulate because increase the number of finite elements means a not negligible increase of calculations time but it decreases the associated error which can be decisive. 

Meanwhile, the three-dimensional model showed must be seen as an approach to the next step of simulation in which is expected to find a way to make the fluid dynamics, thermodynamics and mass transport line up in the same model with all restrictions of the software and hardware already mentioned. 

Also, it is expected in the future to analysis what happen with other elements in the system such as oxygen, iron and copper in which would be appreciated the formation, dynamics and interaction between the phases into the reactor. 

Anyway, it is shown that the new continuous converting process in packed bed is an efficient tool to desulfurizing copper from smelting stage but still needs to be studied to fully understand the process involved.

### **ABSTRACT** 

In consideration to important changes in the composition of the concentrate to process in the Outotec Flash Furnace, the Chuquicamata Smelter of Codelco-Chile has recently carried out successive industrial tests, processing concentrates of low calorific value with high concentration of gangue, by using olivine slag. The traditional processing of this type of concentrates in Chuquicamata’s Flash Furnace is via fayalite slag system, which generates a sharp increase in viscosity of the slag associated with high copper losses, foaming phenomena and other operational problems. 

The partial replacement of silica by limestone flux in order to change the slag system and achieve levels of CaO in the slag in the range of 2.5 to 5%, allowed to efficiently process concentrates characterized by lower pyrite levels (up to 18% in comparison to the traditional average levels of 27% FeS2) and a high proportion of gangue material (14% gangue, traditionally around 9%). This condition achieved average copper values in the slag of less than 1.5%, for CaO contents of around 2.5%, maintaining the copper losses in the slag to historic levels, despite the adverse operating conditions imposed by the quality of the concentrate. 

The addition of limestone, to achieve levels higher than 3% CaO, showed a significant decrease in the distribution of the arsenic toward the matte phase, and better results in terms of copper losses for mattes of around 62% Cu. Therefore, for concentrates with low pyrite content and high gangue levels, olivine type of slags becomes an interesting option to be used.

#### **Effect of the CaOcontent in fayalite slag** 

During the last years several researchers have put interest in investigate the use CaO and its effect in the CaO-FeO-SiO2 system, known as olivine slag. The promising properties of this slag allow to solve industrial problems associated with the use of the iron-silica and iron-calcium slag’s [1-2], and also considers its application in the development of the new technologies such as continuous converting [3-4] and direct process to produce blister copper [5]. The first studies using olivine slag were carried out by Takeda [6-7] at equilibrium with copper matte (10<sup>-12</sup> to 10<sup>-6</sup> atm _P_ O2) at temperatures from 1473 to 1673 K. The results showed that the dissolution of Cu in the slag decreases with increasing CaO content, which is in agreement with the results of other researchers [6-8]. Kim and Sohn [9] reported the effect of addition of CaO, Al2O3 and MgO on the solubility of Copper in iron-silica slag, in the same range of pressures used by Takeda. Kongoly and Yazawa [10] studied the system CaO-SiO2-FeO slag for O2 partial pressures between (10<sup>-8</sup> to 10<sup>-6</sup> atm.), validating the results with experimental data from previous studies [11]. Henao and Itagaki [12] determined the activity coefficients for the same system at O2 partial pressures between 10<sup>-9</sup> to 10<sup>-4</sup> atm at temperatures in the range of 1573-1673 K. 

Concerning to the behavior of impurities in CaO systems, Yazawa et al. [8] studied the removal of the As and Sb, reporting that this slag is much better for the removal this impurities than fayalite slag. Kim and Sohn [9], reported that at low concentrations of CaO (up 4%)in iron-silica slag the distribution coefficients of As, Sb and Bi increased, but for higher CaO content the coefficients remains unchanged. 

The effect of the density, viscosity, temperature and composition of the slag were studied by Utigard and Warczok [13] for the system FeO-Fe2O3-SiO2. Sichen and Seetharaman [14] measured the viscosity of the slag in the ternary CaO-FeO-SiO2, varying the CaO content between 5.5 to 45.5 wt%, FeO 10- 70 wt% at 1423-1753. Kondratiev and Jak [15] based on the Urbain model proposed a new model to describe the viscosity of liquid slag in equilibrium with metallic Fe for a wide range of compositions and temperatures. The results showed that the viscosity decreases with increasing CaO content.

### **CONCLUSIONS** 

1. The substitution of flux to modify the Flash Furnace slag system demonstrated to be a feasible alternative for the processing of concentrates with high silica contents. The results showed that 3% of CaO in the slag decreased the viscosity, with copper contents in FF slag of around 1.8%. 

2. The best results for copper losses in the slag were obtained for CaO in the slag around 2%, (with specific values of the order of 1.0% Cu in slag), for matte grades between 58 to 62% copper. For higher matte grades (66% to 68% Cu), the common values of Cu in slag around 1.5%. 

3. Arsenic distribution in the metal phase decreases, increasing the arsenic in the gas phase with CaO content slag. Antimony content in the slag is almost independent of the CaO content in the slag.
